clue.text: Agree about short fur at last?

indicators.note: about tells us one word goes round the other, so the agreeing word wraps the fur

parts.note: to agree is to tally, as two accounts do

indicators.note: short means the fur's word is cut off before its final letter

parts.note: ermine is the white winter fur of the stoat

explanation.surface: Someone finally agrees on a matter concerning a fur cut too short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims the fur by its last letter, and 'about' wraps the agreeing word round what is left. The question mark flags a playful definition: something done terminally comes at the very end.
explanation.definitionFit: Terminally can mean in a way that comes at the end or final stage, so the definition is a loose, playful synonym.

indicators.note: put out suggests something disturbed or thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Pears are being thrown out onto the lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' rearranges only PEARS, to ESPAR; 'to' is then added as it stands. 'Put out to grass' reads as one idiom for retirement.
explanation.definitionFit: Esparto is a tough Spanish grass used for making paper and rope.

clue.text: Agreement I'm reversing to reveal position

indicators.note: reversing tells us the whole run of letters is read backwards

parts.note: a nod is a sign of agreement
I'm contracted to its letters, dropping the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone reverses their agreement to disclose where they stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversing' turns NODIM into MIDON. MID-ON is a cricket fielding position near the bowler on the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: Mid-on is a named fielding position in cricket.

clue.text: Non-U duke captured by female bushranger

indicators.note: captured by means one piece is held inside another

parts.note: Nelly is a female name

indicators.note: Non-U tells us the letter U is removed from the next word

parts.note: duke taken as written, before the U goes

explanation.surface: A duke who is not upper-class is seized by a woman bushranger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Non-U' is British slang for not upper-class; here it says drop the U from the duke, and 'captured by' sets what remains inside the woman's name. Ned Kelly was a famous Australian outlaw.
explanation.definitionFit: Ned Kelly was a notorious nineteenth-century Australian outlaw, the classic bushranger.

indicators.note: deployed means arranged into a new position, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The most charming porter is posted at a railway station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deployed' rearranges LOVELIEST and PORTER. Liverpool Street is a major London railway terminus.
explanation.definitionFit: Liverpool Street is a mainline railway terminus in the City of London.

indicators.note: wanders suggests moving about aimlessly, so the letters of the name are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man called Rodney roams about over yonder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanders' rearranges the six letters of RODNEY.
explanation.definitionFit: Yonder is an old-fashioned word for at that distant place.

indicators.note: head points to the first letter of the snake's word

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river; the Ure is a Yorkshire river

explanation.surface: A snake's-head fritillary is a flower that looks fine.
explanation.walkthrough: S is the head of 'Snake's'. 'flower' is crossword shorthand for a river; the Ure runs through Yorkshire. Snake's-head is a real flower, which hides the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Sure and OK both express agreement or certainty as casual replies.

clue.text: Focus attention on small round container

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Focus attention on small round container (9)': S (small) + POT (round container) gives only SPOT, and no clue word supplies LIGHT; the clue looks cut short and no search found the full text.
annotationWithheld.clue: Focus attention on small round container

clue.text: Eastern joiner going up in train

indicators.note: going up in a down clue means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a uniter is one who joins things together

explanation.surface: An eastern carpenter climbs aboard a train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going up' reverses EUNITER to give RETINUE. 'Joiner' looks like a carpenter but means anything that unites.
explanation.definitionFit: A train is a body of followers attending an important person, as a retinue is.

indicators.note: little tells us only a small part of the words that follow is taken, the run across them

explanation.surface: Murphy has a small Christmas pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of 'Christmas' into 'pudding'. MURPHY is slang for a potato, from the Irish surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Murphy and spud are both informal words for a potato.

indicators.note: supplied by suggests the furniture is made from the vendor's words, worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Furniture is delivered by a former seller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supplied by' rearranges PAST VENDOR. A davenport is a small writing desk (in American usage, a sofa).
explanation.definitionFit: Davenports are writing desks with a sloping top, a kind of household furnishing.

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of the word outside

parts.note: a spectrum is a full range of something

explanation.surface: A colour that lies at first just beyond the visible spectrum.
explanation.walkthrough: O is the first letter of 'outside'; RANGE follows. The surface tempts us to think of light outside the visible band.
explanation.definitionFit: Orange is a hue between red and yellow.

clue.text: Fish and chips not started before wine is provided

indicators.note: before places the shortened chips ahead of the fish
not started means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: chips are fries in American usage
a ling is a long, cod-like sea fish

explanation.surface: Fish and chips are served before the wine arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not started' drops the first letter of the chips, and 'before' sets that shortened word ahead of the fish, against the order of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Riesling is a white grape variety and the dry or sweet white made from it.

clue.text: Elvis seen on Greek island — say nothing!

parts.note: Kos, also spelt Cos, is a Greek island in the Dodecanese
to say is to tell
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Elvis is spotted on a Greek island, but keep quiet about it!
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a first name standing for the full name: Elvis Costello, the English singer-songwriter, not Presley.
explanation.definitionFit: Elvis Costello is the stage name of the British singer Declan MacManus.

clue.text: Make an inventory, as rustlers do

explanation.surface: Cattle thieves are listing their possessions.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking stock is the standard phrase for counting what a shop holds; rustlers literally take livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: To count goods on hand is stocktaking; cattle thieves seize farm animals, which are also called stock.

clue.text: FBI agents given lowdown about spymaster

indicators.note: about tells us the information word wraps round the spy chief

parts.note: gen is British slang for information, the lowdown
M is the head of the secret service in the James Bond stories

explanation.surface: FBI agents are briefed on a spy chief.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British slang for information; 'about' puts it round M, Bond's spymaster.
explanation.definitionFit: G-men, short for government men, was the American slang name for Federal Bureau of Investigation officers.

clue.text: Single us out? That's not fair!

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are thrown out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A protest at being singled out: it's unjust!
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges SINGLE and US. 'Not fair' means not beautiful, not unjust, which the surface hides.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair here means good-looking, so a lack of beauty is plainness or homeliness.

clue.text: Maximum resentment, by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it tells us the word is one that is pronounced like the resentment word

parts.note: pique is a feeling of irritation or resentment

explanation.surface: The utmost resentment, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: PIQUE is pronounced the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A peak is the highest point or level, the top.

parts.note: to choose by vote is to elect
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: Pick a painter for a Greek play.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, a member of the Royal Academy, is the crossword standard for an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Electra is a tragedy by Sophocles, and another by Euripides.

explanation.surface: Paper tapers are being kept on board ship.
explanation.walkthrough: A spill is a thin strip of wood or paper for lighting a fire; lighters are also flat-bottomed barges.
explanation.definitionFit: Spills are used to kindle flames, an example of things that ignite; lighters are barges that ferry cargo to ships.

parts.note: rum is a British informal word for odd or strange
a Pole is a European, a native of Poland

explanation.surface: A strange European lawyer appears on television.
explanation.walkthrough: Rumpole of the Bailey was a long-running British TV drama about a London barrister.
explanation.definitionFit: Horace Rumpole is the fictional advocate of the series by John Mortimer.

clue.text: Part of flower or fish with equal sides

parts.note: a carp is a freshwater fish

indicators.note: sides points to the first and last letters of the word equal

explanation.surface: A flower part, or a fish whose sides are the same.
explanation.walkthrough: The first and last letters of 'equal' are E and L.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpel is the female reproductive organ of a bloom, holding the ovary.

clue.text: Begin again, cradling a little dicky bird

indicators.note: cradling means holding something inside, as in arms

parts.note: to begin again is to restart

indicators.note: a little means just a small piece of the word, its first letter

explanation.surface: Start over, holding a small birdie.
explanation.walkthrough: D, a little of 'dicky', sits inside RESTART. 'Dicky bird' is a nursery word for a bird, so the definition hides in a phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The redstart is a small songbird with a reddish tail.

parts.note: in means fashionable or trendy
Basil Hume was a Roman Catholic cardinal, Archbishop of Westminster

explanation.surface: A fashionable cardinal is laid to rest.
explanation.walkthrough: Cardinal Basil Hume led the Catholic church in England and Wales until 1999.
explanation.definitionFit: To inhume is to inter a body in the ground.

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A rather remarkable dragon or other beast.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft gave the definition as 'or monster', but 'or' is only a link; the definition is 'monster'. The Hydra was the many-headed serpent slain by Heracles.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hydra is a many-headed serpent of Greek myth, a classic mythical beast.

indicators.note: fresh suggests something new, a new arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: A gloomy person loathes fresh air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh' rearranges MOPER and HATES. It looks like part of 'fresh air' but is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Atmosphere is the air of a place or the mood surrounding it.

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: A fall gives the doctor something to do.
explanation.walkthrough: OP is opus, a musical work.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop is to descend or plummet.

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Is there a rabbit in the hospital kitchen?
explanation.walkthrough: To rabbit, in British slang, is to chatter on at length, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: To rabbit on is British slang for to chatter or natter.

clue.text: It makes us tolerate an indolent person

indicators.note: makes suggests the letters are made into something new, rearranged

explanation.surface: Something that makes us put up with a lazy individual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' rearranges US TOLERATE. In the Odyssey, the lotus-eaters lived in dreamy idleness.
explanation.definitionFit: In Homer's Odyssey, those who ate the lotus fruit lost all will to work, hence a byword for a sluggard.
